articles.title: Motorola Signature 27 demand pushes US delivery dates into December
articles.excerpt: A good problem to have for a $1,600 smartphone.
articles.body: TL;DR Motorola lists a December 8 shipping date for the Signature 27, while Best Buy shows December 11 deliveries or no stock. Motorola has confirmed that higher-than-expected demand is behind the revised shipping timelines. Some early buyers could still receive their phones ahead of the November 26 US retail launch. A $1,600 Motorola phone proving harder to get hold of than expected isn’t something many would have predicted a year ago. Yet that’s the situation facing the Motorola Signature 27 , the company’s big-ticket challenger to Samsung, Google, and Apple in the US. Demand has exceeded Motorola’s expectations, and new buyers may have to wait until December for their phones to arrive. As spotted by 9to5Google , shipping dates for the Signature 27 have slipped into December.

articles.title: Azure DevOps Crash Course (Part 7): Docker, Azure Container Registry and Container Deployments
articles.excerpt: The first time someone explained Docker to me, they said: "It is like shipping your laptop to production, but only the parts that matter." I laughed, but it stuck with me. Our Todo API currently runs…
articles.body: The first time someone explained Docker to me, they said: "It is like shipping your laptop to production, but only the parts that matter." I laughed, but it stuck with me. Our Todo API currently runs on App Service with the .NET runtime that Azure provides. That works great. But sometimes you want full control over exactly what runs: the OS packages, the .NET version, everything. That is where containers come in. In Part 6 we sorted out configuration and secrets. Today we: Write a Dockerfile for the Todo API Build the image in Azure Pipelines Push it to Azure Container Registry (ACR) Run the container on App Service What you need to know before the code A Dockerfile is a recipe. Docker follows it and produces an image : your app plus everything it needs to run.

articles.title: How to Audit a Blog Archive When You Don’t Know How the Content Was Written
articles.excerpt: Audit your blog archive with practical steps to verify claims, investigate AI concerns, improve weak articles, and decide what to update or remove. A new content manager inherits a blog with hundreds…
articles.body: Audit your blog archive with practical steps to verify claims, investigate AI concerns, improve weak articles, and decide what to update or remove. A new content manager inherits a blog with hundreds of published articles. Some have clear bylines and source notes; others arrived through agencies or contributors who no longer work with the business. The writing varies, references are inconsistent, and nobody can confidently explain how every article was produced. Reviewing the archive requires more than guessing which passages might have involved AI. The practical goal is to determine which pages readers can rely on, which need work, and which no longer deserve publication. Questions about authorship belong in that review, alongside accuracy, attribution, usefulness, and accountability.

One template, two live apps — FixIt Auto (auto repair) and BrightSmile Dental — each with its own dashboard, plus a self-serve kit so any shop owner can spin up their own page in minutes. articles.title: Designing a Rewards Store: How Cashback Wallets, Points and Gift Card Redemption Fit Together
articles.excerpt: Most rewards products start simple: "give users some cashback". Within a few months the team is dealing with points that expire, vouchers that run out of stock, partial redemptions and users asking wh…
articles.body: Most rewards products start simple: "give users some cashback". Within a few months the team is dealing with points that expire, vouchers that run out of stock, partial redemptions and users asking where their money went. The difference between a rewards program people trust and one they abandon is mostly in how the wallet and the rewards store are designed. Here is a practical way to structure it. 1. One ledger, several balances Keep a single append only ledger table and derive every balance from it. Each row has a user, an amount, a currency type and a reason: type meaning cashback real money, withdrawable to UPI or bank points program currency, only redeemable in the store bonus_points promotional points with an expiry date Never update a balance column in place.

The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power Season 3 finale, titled “The Doom of Men,” closes out a season that rejuvenated the flailing series with the promise that Sauron’s worst is yet to come in the just announced Season 4 . articles.body: SpaceX launched another classified mission for the U.S. Space Force (USSF) today (Nov. 24), sending an unknown payload toward orbit from California. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from Vandenberg Space Force Base's Space Launch Complex-4E at TK11:08 a.m. ET (1508 GMT) , carrying the U.S. Space Force's USSF-266 mission. It was the fourth mission SpaceX has launched for the military branch this month. articles.title: On this day in space! Nov. 24, 1947: The US Navy launches the 1st Aerobee sounding rocket, but it didn't reach space
articles.excerpt: On Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space. Here's why it mattered.
articles.body: On Nov. 24, 1947, the U.S. Navy launched the first Aerobee rocket into the sky, but it never reached space. Aerobee was a suborbital sounding rocket designed to study Earth's atmosphere . After World War 2, the United States started reusing erman V-2 rockets for this kind of research. When they started running out of V-2 rockets , the United States constructed its own rockets that were similar but cheaper to build and to launch. In the weeks leading up to the first Aerobee mission, three test flights were launched. Those tests used a dummy version of Aerobee with a live booster to see if the two stages would separate properly. On Aerobee's first real flight, the rocket flew about 35 miles high. That's below the 62-mile (100 kilometers) upper limit for the boundary of space .
